components.name: camera
components.method: MoGe prior + known-geometry PnP profiles, background rotation and stationary-object camera anchors
components.note: Refined camera excludes partial-mask depth hump, max translation2.54cm. Focal regularized1050px; monocular sensitivity retained.

components.name: objects_6d
components.method: Blender geometry, SAM3/SAM2 and physically constrained render-and-compare

components.name: hand_motion
components.method: HaWoR plus mandatory MANO optimizer owned copy, all778 vertices, anatomical opposed contact and geometry-derived separation; independent installed validators

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

scene.model: Full provided Marvin Wuji MJCF, both arms/hands and original collision geometry, with a single plug, table, floor, and column.

plug.state_frame: Housing centre, +Z toward blade tips, +Y across the blade gap. Identity object/body frame.
plug.geometry: Station housing and two blade OBJ parts from given/recon. Exact specified dimensions and axes.
plug.physical_prior: The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
plug.contact: Housing and two blades have separate convex collision meshes. Elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solref 0.012 s / damping ratio 1, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001].

reference.method: White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

body.arm: Measured-seed DLS IK, 1 and 0.2 position/rotation weights, eight updates per 100 Hz tick, a soft home preference and approach-to-column rejection using the collision capsules. Right arm 5-degree-margin limits, 20 mm and 0.075 rad per tick sent-target caps, published jump and box checks, per-joint command rate capped at 3.1416 rad/s. Models the joint-specific delay and low-pass response and impedance relative to command velocity. Joint torques use full physical contact generalized forces with a 30 ms external-torque estimator. The parked left side has its original collision masks.
body.hand: Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise.
body.sensor: Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform independent x/y offsets ±10 mm and blade yaw ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, X-up on the supported face.
initial_conditions.start_check: Hold controller uses the reset palm so the entire hold check, including any ramp rows, can test a stationary hand. Candidate evaluation simulates the actual package start ramp.

body.limitations: The kinematic replay has large positional errors and brief hand–plug overlap, and uses a visualization-only aperture. It is not evidence of physical feasibility. Ramp lag at the recommended start is 32.7 mm, above the station example 18–25 mm, so the first action needs margin. No measured glove friction or plug mass from the station. Independent parity is pending for any parallel training backend.

body.text: The reconstructed approach yaw is outside the robot's reachable branch. The wrist-only retarget improves reach but still has a 44 mm median positional error and 3.7 mm maximum overlap in a kinematic replay. I am fitting an opposed pinch on the plug's width faces, then testing whether differential finger motion can rotate it about the width axis while keeping the wrist excursion close to the video. The first static fit touched both sides in some rollouts, but all grasps lost opposition at lift in the tested draw. The next test increases inward pad travel and uses gentler lift.

body.method: privileged geometry fit and contact-physics waypoint search
body.hypothesis: An opposed width-face pinch with added preload and synchronized leftward wrist travel will lift and carry the plug across randomized starts. The local baseline sometimes reached the goal but still showed late reorientation and intermittent loss of opposition.
body.observed: The demonstration keeps finger opposition during the turn. The local baseline attained 5.6 degrees from upright during opposed contact on one draw, then lost that contact before stable placement.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop

body.text: In r0008 the feasibility baseline lifted 32/32 and passed no turns. In seed 457221813 the montage shows the plug on the table by 10.03 s, and the sampled contacts show a loss of thumb opposition by 6.183 s while it is airborne. Seed 351492938 also lost opposition during the turn, and exceeded a deployed finger limit by 0.040 rad. In local full-rate traces the initial opening stroke drives the desired turn, but the pad opens before the table takes the load. The new controller splits that stroke into active roll, maintained contact during descent, and release. I will also test a stiffer physical finger stop against the documented 0.02 rad allowance. Policy weights still start from scratch.

body.text: Dynamic CPU/Warp outcome parity passed on 128 matched full-range starts with the same fixed feasibility plan: 8/128 CPU and 11/128 GPU, zero hardware violations in both. This was a 13 s plan plus settling comparison, separate from the 60 s gates. The end-to-end PPO experiment will use the matched GPU scene, a deployable observation history and reference-progress rewards. Mid-skill curriculum resets use physically realised simulator qpos/qvel and contact phases aligned to the reconstruction. The PPO learner reads no controller actions, and no weights are initialized from feasibility rollouts. Budget the first PPO configuration 60 million active steps, with CPU checkpoint tests and continued training if the curve is still improving.

body.text: Task feasibility is proven. Begin the 60-million-active-step PPO experiment from random weights, with the matched GPU simulator, state-only curriculum reset bank, default noisy sensor, and no demonstration or controller actions in training.

Stopped the first PPO launch after the initial batch produced non-finite reward and loss values. It did not yield an evaluated policy. The training loop now detects numerical divergence in each Warp world, charges a failed episode, resets that world, and checks advantages before optimization. The CPU evaluator and criteria are unchanged. Restart from random weights.

The restarted PPO run has finite losses and active-state KL near 0.01, with early returns improving and occasional completion from late curriculum resets. Launch a second random seed with the same PPO configuration on an idle GPU to measure seed sensitivity. Select any recorded evaluation on simulator results, using the frozen task gate for every kept package.

body.text: Task baseline r0022 has valid contract logs and no hardware violations. In seed 1570346490 at 2.30 s, the fingers reach the plug, but by 10.00 s the side view shows the fingers above the plug with its housing still on the table. Test a closer pre-grasp package start as a parallel PPO experiment while the two recommended-start seeds continue. The pose held without contact or stops on all 64 development draws and maintained full reported visibility. The reward, PPO architecture, full plug start distribution and physics are the same. Budget 30 million active steps for this branch.

The alternate pre-grasp exposed a GPU ramp parity bug. Its quaternion descriptor was in the opposite hemisphere from the reset quaternion, and the GPU linear blend took the long path. Match the CPU sign choice before the blend. The corrected GPU ramp then passed 256 randomized hold starts with no stop, limit excursion, or contact, and full reported visibility at hold. Restart the branch from scratch. The first alternate-start launch produced no evaluated policy.

body.reflection: Continued the same PPO configuration. On 64 full CPU episodes, all four stages remained at zero with no hardware violations and no stops. Largest rise remained 1.9 mm and unsupported opposition was absent. Next examine preload and supported pinch quality while completing the method budget.

body.text: r0022 montage seed 1281518469 shows an early digit tap with the housing supported, followed by a rise of the hand alone. In matched dev seed 8173501, the 6.09M policy peaked at 0.32 N of opposing normal force, the 10.33M checkpoint had no opposed force in its first 6 s, and the feasible fixed motion sustained 3 to 5 N with nearly antiparallel normals. Binary simultaneous contact rewards incidental taps. A proposed acquisition reward uses the simulated minimum opposed normal component, capped at 2.5 N, and qualifies the existing acquisition bonus after three 30 Hz samples above 1.4 N. A same-rays plan check across 24 starts averaged +28.99 versus hold -0.79 and random -2.18, with 24 qualifying plan lifts and zero plan hardware violations. This is training-only reward guidance and changes no policy input or evaluation rule. The two original seeds continue their 60M step budget. The 10.33M assessment is iteration r0025.

Physical reset audit in 1323 snapshots found a curriculum defect. Resetting hand targets to measured angles unloads the contact before learning can act. After a 0.1 s hold, 167/312 turn states and 17/175 carry states retained unsupported opposition. A training-only initialization solves a friction-wrench balance from each snapshot geometry and maps it through contact Jacobians and the modeled finger servos. It uses no demonstrated or controller actions. On the same randomized starts, 312/312 turn and 138/175 carry states now retain unsupported opposition at 0.1 s, with no hardware violations or stops. Save these actuator memory states in a separate reset bank. Run a concurrent single-variable curriculum repair with the original start, reward, domain randomization and PPO settings for 60M active steps. Predict lift first through better mid-state learning and later turn. Continue the original seeds to their budgets for comparison. r0022 seed 1281518469 shows lack of sustained opposition before the hand rises.

body.text: The r0025 actor was replayed on 16 matched dev starts for 8 s with previous targets in the history replaced by measured pose/joints. Its command integration still uses the contract previous targets. Original made positive-depth contact in 13/16 and had 1.6 mm max rise with no unsupported opposition. Masked made contact in 16/16, one episode reached 21.2 mm maximum rise with 0.183 s of unsupported opposition, and both had no stops or limit violations. This is an input-ablation diagnostic of the same learned checkpoint and is not a task-gate result. It suggests the two histories may encourage target following independent of contact. Assess target dropout or a measured-hand-relative action encoding after current budgets, alongside the observed failure to load the pinch.

Correction to r0029: 21.2 mm was the maximum rise over all masked episodes (seed 8173513, no opposition). The qualifying lift was a different episode, seed 8173529, with 12.9 mm rise and 0.183 s of unsupported opposition. Masked lift count 1/16 versus 0/16 on this short diagnostic.

body.text: A reach audit found the wrist reward itself encourages an infeasible approach. Across the fixed 64 CPU starts, the uncalibrated frame-73 waypoint has median IK error 66.08 mm and only 3/64 satisfy 10 mm and 0.05 rad. The fitted pinch geometry gives 64/64 and median error 0.31 mm with a fixed palm-frame correction. Applying that correction throughout destroys reachability late, so the proposed reward fades it out across frames 130 to 148. The blended waypoints are reachable in 64/64 at frames 73 to 140, 61/64 at frame 149 and 43/64 at frame 162, versus 3/64 to 56/64 at the early frames, 56/64 and 35/64 at the last two. The object references stay reconstructed; the pool then selects by start heading as well as position. This is a wrist reward correction prepared for after the active budgets. See experiment/media/reference_alignment.json.

r0034 rejected the palm-history ablation. Candidate had 3/32 lifts in the initial sample, 4 candidate-only lifts versus zero incumbent-only on 96 paired draws (p=0.0625), zero full success, and two paired hardware violations versus zero. I reviewed both failure montages. In seed 209181378 at 2.30 s the digits bracket the housing but by 10 s there is a visible gap; the trace reports no unsupported opposition and 10.2 mm rise. In seed 493618404 the housing tilts under the finger and stays supported, later leaving the grasp region; trace reports 60.75 s of environment contact and no airborne grip. The mask improved interaction but did not reliably sustain a pinch. An updated training-only acquisition reward also preserves the starting blade posture through the pinch so table-assisted tipping does not qualify. Benchmarked on matched physical commands, 24/24 still qualified for the reward lift; mean return +29.12 versus hold -0.79 and random -2.18. No task criteria or frozen evaluator changes. Continue the active budgets.

body.text: Matched deterministic mid-state diagnostics on 48 settled states per phase, from the reset pool. These are six-second GPU tests using training stage signals, not independent deployment episodes. From pre-contact approaches the 10.33M original and 12.21M settled actors reached the training lift phase boundary in 20/48 and 19/48 without stops. From carry states they reached the training placement condition in 28/48 and 30/48, and from support-transfer states in 47/48 and 48/48. From turn states the original reached placement in 0/48 and the settled actor in 4/48. The full-start CPU tests of both actors have zero qualifying lifts. This locates a large reset-to-grasp gap while showing that late-phase signals can be learned. Preserve full-start training and focus the next change on reach and contact. Raw counts are in experiment/media/mid_policy_intervals.json.

body.text: The fixed pre-grasp experiment exhausted its 30M budget at 30,020,875 steps. Median return in the last three five-million step bins was 2.92, 2.99 and 2.96. The last 10,182 full training episodes had zero lifts and turns despite 9,937 binary opposition events. Its final 64 CPU episodes had zero lifts, six hardware violation episodes, four arm collision stops and two torque stops. Move GPU 3 to a fresh PPO branch for 40M steps with the same package start, network, randomization and reset pool. Batch two reward improvements because the audited acquisition failures support both. r0034 seed 209181378 loses contact after the early grasp attempt and seed 493618404 tips the plug while still supported. Qualify the pinch only with sustained opposed normal force and preserved blade orientation. Also replace the unreachable early wrist target with the calibrated reference from r0035. The combined dry check earns +26.51 on physical plans vs -0.79 hold and -2.18 random, with 23/24 plan lifts and zero plan violations. Predict more lift events and less table tipping. The original seed 8117 now shows 64/64 dev lifts and 15 turns, so it continues without change to at least its original 60M budget.

body.text: r0047 initial sample on the 37.72M actor was 32/32 lifts, 9/32 turns and zero carry or placement, with one finger violation. The gate extended and the paired comparison failed contract checks, including a late palm tracking excursion and an arm-limit trace. The incumbent remains r0022. Reviewed both failure montages. In seed 959012081 at 2.30 s the plug is held and still oblique. By 10 s it lies on the table behind the hovering hand. It had 1.33 s unsupported opposition and ended y=-0.514 m. Seed 1280450212 also lifts and releases before a qualifying upright turn, leaving y=-0.427 m. Local 40.76M data then show two upright final placements after supported movement with prior loss of the turning grip. The next reward diagnostic adds signed progress toward goal y under unsupported opposition and resets the attempt on early support or lost grip. A separate 60 s curriculum test can address late actions and contract stability. The original seed continues because its turn curve is still improving.

body.text: Numerical arm-limit audit after r0047. I tested a separate copy of the CPU scene with more rigid 4 ms arm joint-limit constraints and the same deployed ranges. Eight short-listed 37.72M policy traces produced byte-identical results in v2 and this variant with our local sensor seeds, so they did not recreate the gate extension issue. On the eight worst original 3.03M traces, the added stiffness reduced max measured arm excursions from 0.279 to 0.646 rad to 0.079 to 0.390 rad beyond a deployed limit. All eight still exceed the gate tolerance of 0.05 rad. Keep v2 for training and evaluation. Do not treat altered scene data as passed. Since later policy actions can enter those configurations, plan to learn the full 60 s horizon and monitor measured tracking before spending a new gate. A signed +Y reward with continuous-grip checks earns +26.23 on fixed physical plans and -0.79 on hold, and awards all 24 lifts. It makes carry after early support fail the training attempt.

body.text: Original seed 8117 reached 60,049,849 active steps. The full-start CPU checkpoint lifts 63/64 and turns 51/64, with zero qualifying carry/release and placement, seven hardware violations and two torque stops. Across the last two step bins stochastic releases dropped from 60 of 12,136 to 21 of 12,832, while median return grew from 32.97 to 52.65. Change the reward after the fixed budget because ordered task completion is flat despite higher reward. Continue from the saved PPO-only 60M actor, critic and optimizer on GPU 1 for about 35M additional steps. r0047 seed 959012081 drops its first held plug on the right. r0053 seed 8173561 opens before support and seed 8173557 leaves the zone during descent. The reward now pays signed +Y progress within the grasp, aborts a broken attempt, pays every sparse phase once, and steers descent 15 mm inside the zone. The physical 24-start dry check earns +26.69 vs hold -0.79 and random -2.18, with all plan lifts, two releases and zero plan hardware violations. Predict more stable carry and release. The training rollout horizon and deployment start remain the original configuration.

body.reflection: Original PPO seed 8117 completed the 60M budget. Local CPU tests show 63 lifts and 51 turns over 64 full starts, zero carry/release or placement, seven hardware-limit episodes and two torque stops. Task completion stalled while early-stage reward increased. Freeze this PPO checkpoint as parent for transport and safety comparisons.

body.text: Seed 8118 completed 60,062,485 steps. The last 11,941 full training episodes have zero lifts, turns or releases, median return 2.82. Its final full CPU sample also has zero qualifying stages, with five hardware violations and five torque stops. Use its freed GPU for a 35M-step continuation from the frozen seed-8117 60M PPO checkpoint. Test late control under a 35 percent mixture of 60 s deployment starts and a static task palm box x[.245,.56], y[-.49,.12], z[-.255,.11] m. Batch both changes for safety because the r0047 late gate tracking and arm-limit errors occur beyond the 15 s training horizon and the old actor often sends late x=.19 or y=-.62 commands outside the task corridor. Our feasible physical path spans x .302 to .480 and y -.350 to -.090. The 60 s mix passed a 64-world finite-batch smoke test, and NumPy/Torch action agreement is below 1.2e-7 in both boxes. Predict fewer hardware violations and fewer contract tracking errors. The carry-reward comparison on GPU 1 uses the same parent weights.

body.text: Transport resets from the PPO actor itself may reduce the gap between its learned turn and later placement. On 80 training-only start draws with the seed-8117 60M package, collect physically supported state traces for 14 s. Keep pose and velocity from safe rollouts in true lifted turn intervals and after qualifying active turn, and keep no actions. The new bank adds 773 turn and 183 upright carry snapshots to 2,279 total. Recompute simulated actuator strain from contact geometry. In a 2,279-start randomized GPU hold audit, 1,067 of 1,085 turn states and 267 of 358 carry states retain airborne opposition at 0.1 s with zero stops or violations in those groups. Plan a continuation with these mid-states after the settled-reset budget if the deployment actor still fails the transport link. All gates continue to start at the deployment pose.

body.text: Tested whether the 63.07M carry actor reaches an arm limit after the upright turn. From 58 qualified upright snapshots, hold the measured grip transform and ask the station IK to move the body centre to (.414, -.057, -.272). All 58 fit within 10 mm and .05 rad at their observed wrist heading, and the same count fits with +15 to +40 deg yaw about world vertical. Negative yaw is mostly unreachable from that branch. Median farthest upright held y is -.170 m, so plain arm reach appears sufficient for the missing translation. This is a static kinematic test and supplies no controller actions. Prefer more training of the transport reward over changing the wrist mapping. Details in experiment/media/transport_reach63.json.

body.text: r0068 main gate evaluated 32 lifts, 25 turns and no later stages with zero violations, then the paired extension flagged a late arm-limit and measured wrist-speed trace at t=53.43 s. Keep r0022 as incumbent. I reviewed both gate montages. Seed 1673894843 holds the plug at 2.30 s and lets it fall back below the fingers by 25.40 s; final y=-0.283 m. Seed 743174 repeatedly changes the plug angle in the grasp and ends y=-0.182 m. The newer local carry checkpoint r0070 completes four supported releases. For example seed 8173540 gains support at 7.217 s, opens at 7.250 s and touches again at 7.300 s. This motivates slowing the supported plug, clearing the hand after release and assigning terminal credit only if the goal remains stable at the training horizon.

body.text: The expanded placement-reset pool is ready for a curriculum comparison. A separate 128-start collection using the r0077 PPO actor yielded no complete episodes, so its single local success is sparse. State extraction added 1,170 turn frames, 1,115 upright carry frames and 189 supported placement frames after qualifying carried entry. Total pool 4,753, with no action targets copied. Analytic finger servo preload produces 2,234/2,255 turn and 1,367/1,473 carry states with airborne opposition at 0.1 s, and 378/401 placement states with thumb-opponent contact. All groups had zero stops and hardware violations during the hold audit. Keep full starts in the curriculum and oversample carry and supported release when the acquisition budget frees GPU 3. The targeted failure is r0078 right-side turning and r0071 immediate recontact after support.

body.reflection: 64 CPU starts: 62 lift, 50 turn, five supported releases and one valid success, with 25 limit violations and six stops across the sample. Seed 8173528 leaves the plug at x 0.4225, y -0.0045 at rest for 46.75 seconds after a clean 82.3 degree active turn. The rate and hardware findings do not support a gate.

body.text: r0083 confirms a second independent full CPU completion at the 78.18M placement checkpoint, seed 8173528. The plug rests upright inside the zone from 13.25 s to 60 s with no hand recontact, stop or violation. In the same batch 25/64 episodes violate the finger limits. At 60 Hz ten show the first limit crossing in the sampled trace, eight with no plug contact. The middle finger abduction joint accounts for six of the ten. At t=19.533 in seed 8173502 it crosses the lower limit at -0.322 rad while recent issued targets are -0.244, -0.224, -0.190 rad, all well inside the -0.300 rad hardware limit. Other excursions happen with saturated commands, so extra target margin alone cannot explain or resolve these results. Keep the trained configuration active through its planned budget and check late noncontact arm and finger motion in subsequent checkpoints. Task v2 remains frozen.

body.reflection: The long-horizon continuation achieved 64/64 lifts and 57 turns in the CPU batch. It makes no supported release or stable final placement, stops zero times and exceeds finger limits in three episodes. r0078 remains the incumbent. The long-horizon loss alone does not move the object left consistently after turning.

body.text: The 2 ms diagnostic replay reproduced all 25 limit failures of the placement checkpoint in r0083. Fourteen first crossings affect middle MCP2, all below its -0.300 rad lower limit. At 14 of 25 first crossings there is no normal force above 0.1 N on a hand contact, while at nine crossings the plug touches a hand link. Crossing velocities reach 31.7 rad/s even with issued targets in spec. Several involve the finger snapping through rapidly after prior loads. Carrying eligibility continues to improve while late forced manipulation stays risky. Plan testable action stability or limit-margin shaping only after active branch budgets, with frozen CPU v2 comparisons. Evidence is experiment/ppo_evaluations/place78m/limit_crossings.json.

The 81.20M carry checkpoint now has ten qualifying supported releases in 64 CPU starts. The first split from hand contact near support, inside the zone and with blades up, occurs at 0.145–0.325 m/s linear speed and 0.71–7.66 rad/s spinning across these ten traces. All ten recontact on the next 60 Hz sample. One of the ten, seed 8173537, eventually rests for 1.05 s and is then moved away. A useful follow-up after the carry budget tests supported transfer with bounded approach speed before contact and a settled support dwell before opening. r0078 gate shows absence of leftward carry, so keep carry shaping when testing this distinction.

Acquisition has completed its planned 40M-step run at 40,059,027. The last 11,367 stochastic full starts registered zero opposed acquisition, lifts or turns, with 1,051 limit violations and 369 stops. Full CPU evaluation is in progress. GPU 3 starts a 36M-step weighted transport reset test from the 75,139,084-step PPO parent in r0077, checkpoint SHA-256 51d53553130c…. The parent completed one valid whole episode on 64 CPU starts. r0078 montages show repeated turning short of the goal. The test bundles the carry and settling rewards already measured separately with the long-episode fraction 0.35, the task palm box and r0081 training-only physically settled resets. The mid fraction begins near 0.42 and decays to 0.24 over the budget, with phases weighted 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.35, 0.30. Predictor: more clean supported releases and fewer recontacts on the original full, fresh-start contract-v3 distribution. All actor and critic weights come from the same random-initialized PPO lineage. The reset pool includes joint and object states but no actions. Continue the existing carry, placement and long-horizon comparisons through their own budgets.

body.text: During the 0.4 s before first upright hand-held support in the goal, the median visible fraction never exceeds 0.074 in the ten r0089 carry-release traces. All ten have zero valid camera estimates in that window, the held pose is 1.92–1.99 s old and its position error is 0.201–0.211 m. The two learned completions in r0077 and r0083 are also occluded at the corresponding transition. So are all eight successful fixed-plan CPU parity traces at a visibility fraction of zero. Settled transfer can work with the demonstrated grip despite camera loss. A prospective observation experiment would retain an earlier estimated object-to-palm pose and the hand joint change since that estimate, using only contract pose and proprioception history, with no clock and no change to the action rule. Visibility analysis used only frozen development rollouts and the already recorded fixed-plan diagnostic.

Paired closed-loop check of r0077 across 64 matched nominal start poses. CPU 63 lifts, 61 turns, four releases, one complete, six violations and three stops. GPU 64 lifts, 64 turns, one release, zero complete, two violations and three stops. The default sensor draws differ by backend. Both carry and release rates are small, so this diagnostic shows the manipulation is learned in both backends and release has not generalized. The earlier fixed-plan parity proof r0013 remains the physics comparison. Files are under experiment/policy_parity/carry75m. For the r0092 visibility statistic, the per-trace 0.4 s statistic is a mean rather than a median.

A prospective gentle-transfer reward derived from r0089 and r0087 is ready. It applies up to 0.08 per step of cost for excess speed in the last 60 mm of descent and on hand contact at support inside the goal, then awards 5 once for two near-rest, blades-up samples with both support and hand contact. It leaves the frozen evaluator and execution policy unchanged. In the 24-start dry test, mean rewards were +27.70 for the fixed physical plan, -0.79 hold and -2.18 random. Two plan runs reached the stable terminal and there were zero plan stops or violations. Source experiment/media/gentle_transfer_dry.log. Consider after the active carry or long branch reaches budget with no completion trend.

body.text: Prepare a separate 96-start state-only settlement collection numbered 5168201 through 5168296 using the already measured feasibility controller r0014 on CPU sim v2. These starts are reserved for curriculum diagnostics and are distinct from the development and gate starts. We will report the 96-start controller results and may retain only physical states, motions and reward context around near-rest transfer and just after release. The policy will never train on the source actions or use the controller. By starting some episodes in the released state we can test whether continuing PPO learns to leave an already stood plug untouched.

Integrated the last 80 training updates into reward by term per completed episode. Carry PPO averaged 17.62 signed leftward points (single path cap 7), 11.20 carry points (cap 5), and 7.22 lift-progress points (cap 2), across 12,586 full episodes. Placement averaged 18.79, 13.09 and 8.11 for the same terms across 12,457 full episodes. The active-phase mask turns off when opposition is lost or a trial restarts, so backtracking can avoid repayment and the same translation can earn again. Together with the repeated rolls in r0078, this gives a mechanism for return rising while full completion stays rare. Prepare episode-best bounded progress on lift, trajectory, carry, settlement and retreat while preserving retry, phase and final criteria. This is a reward experiment after an active budget completes, with no evaluator change.

body.text: The observed hardware excursions motivate a prospective training-only limit cost. Penalize measured finger movement toward a limit above 5 rad/s within 35 mrad, measured overshoot beyond 5 mrad and an additional -4 at violation. Give a small cost for arm joints near deployed limits or sustained large measured palm-to-target error. No execution guard, altered stop rule or evaluator change. Dry test on the r0013 fixture yields +23.33 for the physical plans (one stable end, no violations, zero added limit or tracking cost), -0.79 hold and -6.29 random. Proceed with this option only if the release branch continues to show limit problems after its budget.

body.text: Bounded progress dry check on 24 previous nominal fixture starts yields +25.10 physical plan, -0.79 hold and -2.18 random. All 24 plans lift, 10 turn, one settles at the terminal, zero stops or violations. Averaged shaped values are 6.39 leftward, 4.16 carry and 1.16 lift, each below its 7, 5 and 2 single-episode cap. The new account also pays only when a previously unpassed demonstration waypoint is reached. Run a continuation after the first available branch finishes its budget, with the same reset and domain randomization profile as its PPO parent. See experiment/media/progress_once_dry.log.

The 96 training-only settlement collection using the existing privileged feasibility probe yields 59/96 full completions, with no hardware violations or stops. body.reflection: Third distinct complete CPU rollout in the campaign, seed 8173524. It turns the object in the fingers, releases it supported and leaves it at (0.4098, -0.0866, -0.2935) m at zero recorded speed and spin for the terminal period. The batch reaches 63 lifts, 61 turns and one supported release and placement, with ten violation episodes and three stops. Weighted resets still need much more consistency.

body.text: The new state-only pool contains 6,977 states. The 96-start physical controller collection adds 940 turn, 622 upright carry, 366 supported-transfer and 296 post-release snapshots. Randomized GPU hold at 0.1 s shows 693/767 supported-transfer states with opposed contacts and 740/767 still supported. Of 296 post-release states, 288 are upright, supported, within the final goal and stationary without hand contact at 0.1 s, and 295 at 1.0 s. No stage-5 violation or stop. Source and exact diagnostics are in experiment/settlement_curriculum. The bank is prepared for a future curriculum comparison and has not been used in training.

The prospective last-visible observation anchor passed NumPy and Torch parity at 9.54e-7 maximum feature error on 3,600 exact CPU trace observations, including 973 invalid-camera steps retaining an earlier valid pose. A package after 3,124 active PPO smoke steps passed the contract v3 API and time-invariance checks at 0.506 ms p99. The 33 new inputs are derived from earlier pose estimates and measured finger displacement. No full-start performance iteration has used them.

Weight normalization clarification for r0099. The old leftward term pays 7 points per 0.29 m of one-way progress. Across deployment y starts from -0.37 to -0.35 m and the training target -0.057 m, one direct path can earn 7.07–7.56 points. The observed mean 17.62 still exceeds that by more than a factor of two. The proposed bounded potential clamps its full-episode total at 7.

body.text: Finished the planned long-horizon branch at 95,041,537 active steps. The final 7,320 stochastic full starts report 18 releases and zero complete episodes, compared with 27 releases and zero complete in the previous 7,092. The 90.45M and 93.51M CPU checkpoints both had zero turns and later stages after progressing earlier in the budget. This branch is flat or regressing on the required stages. Its final CPU evaluation is in progress. GPU 2 now starts the bounded episode-progress experiment for 38M additional steps from the r0108 transport parent (81,185,190 steps, checkpoint SHA-256 2a94d6446b3c…). Keep its reset pool, weights, full-episode fraction, task box, domain randomization and optimizer. Change only the progress rewards described in r0105 and r0111. A short smoke test completed 7,326 active steps with no divergent world. r0078 seed 2098461065 is still repeatedly rolling a plug short of the goal from 10 to 56.2 s. Predict more supported releases and stable goal states without repeated reward for the same excursion. Carry, placement and transport retain their assigned budgets.

body.text: Completed the carry-only continuation at 95,065,802 active steps. Its final 12,619 stochastic full starts report 35 releases and 19 short-horizon proxy completions, down from 225 and 80 in the prior 12,606. The 87.34M, 90.40M and 93.40M CPU checkpoints complete no whole tasks, and the final CPU test is running. GPU 1 now compares the gentle-transfer reward for 34M steps from the same r0108 transport parent, reset mixture, full-length fraction, task box and DR as the active bounded-progress and baseline transport runs. Only the reward changes. See r0094 for the dry test. The r0078 observations are an incomplete carry and repeated in-hand turning. When the weighted carry can arrive in the goal, the first openings in r0089 still have large speed and all recontact on the next sample. Lowering touchdown speed and rewarding brief settled support should convert more carried entries into quiet releases. Continue the other budgets.

Lift 61, turn 55, violation episodes 27, stops 13. The progression is measurable before the final condition, so continue the planned budget and audit postrelease activity and limits.

body.text: The r0124 release audit matches a qualifying release in each of 12 partial carry episodes. The first openings happen at 0.089–0.148 m/s and 0.83–5.44 rad/s, with all 12 recontacting on the next 60 Hz sample. Seed 8173551 later has two intervals of upright rest in the goal, the longest 14.017–25.383 s. It keeps the plug steady at (0.3530, -0.0137, -0.2935) m, withdraws, then torque-halts with no plug contact while the plug is still at rest. The halt at 20.126 Nm and a limit excursion of 0.05031 rad exclude success. This shows that settling and post-release hardware stability both need evaluation. Files in experiment/ppo_evaluations/progress84m.

body.reflection: The 96.42M placement checkpoint completed one new full CPU episode, seed 8173525, with no violation or stop. It leaves the plug at (0.4316, -0.0419, -0.2935) m at rest for the last 49.83 s. Of 64 starts, 64 lift, 63 turn and six release. Twenty-one episodes violate limits and 19 stop, so this isolated placement is not gate-ready.

body.text: The r0124 seed 8173551 torque-halt decomposition at 25.372 s is entirely joint-limit constraint load at that physics sample: instantaneous +23.26 Nm on J6, filtered +20.13 Nm, with zero external-contact contribution. J6 is already at -1.662 rad, beyond its -1.0 rad deployed bound. It remains a failed episode. A separate CPU copy changes only integration from 2 ms to 1 ms and keeps the 100 Hz controller. The eight selected stress seeds go from eight stops to zero, eight finger violation episodes to two, and seven trajectories beyond the arm limit tolerance to zero. One of four previously clean controls instead halts with 0.839 rad maximum arm excess. There are zero full successes among these 12 revised simulations. Integration step matters but the smaller step alone does not eliminate the defect. Running the fully specified physical feasibility controller locally on 32 separate diagnostic starts before any adoption decision. The registered suites and v2 checks were not modified.

Seventeen hardware violation episodes and eight stops. An early checkpoint does not establish whether the supported dwell bonus will improve stability.

body.text: The independent 2 ms discrete-integrator version of the stress test kept all 12 selected traces within the recorded hardware checks with zero stops, 12 lifts and 11 turns. At 2 ms implicitfast in v2, the eight stress seeds all stop and the four controls stay clean. The discrete run completes zero supported releases or placements in this small stress batch, so this is evidence about integration stability. A new CPU feasibility diagnostic and 128-seed CPU/Warp fixed-plan parity test are underway. The MuJoCo manual describes the discrete solver as using the same effective inertia for constraint resolution and integration, including implicit position stiffness. That is relevant to the arm-limit excursions in r0068 and r0127. The test uses an isolated copy with the same controller and limits. [MuJoCo computation and integrators](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/stable/computation/index.html#integrators)

body.text: The two isolated simulator alternatives each have a contact tradeoff. On the same 32 diagnostic starts the unchanged adaptive physical controller completes 9/32 with 1 ms implicitfast and 4/32 with 2 ms discrete, zero violations or stops for either. All 12 discrete stress traces pass the published replay contract. On another 128 matched fixed-plan starts the discrete CPU and GPU both lift 128 and complete zero full tasks, with zero violations. The official d2s_parity report passes with matching success, violation and drop rates, which does not establish task feasibility. Retain the v2 training and gate while the paired 2 ms baseline tests and policy experiments run. body.reflection: The 93M transport checkpoint has 63 lifts, 61 turns and one supported carry/release. It has no stable placed endpoint, 22 limit violation episodes and six stops. The run retains its 36M-step study budget.

body.text: All five distinct completed local CPU rollouts pass the standard v3 state-log replay, with no stop or hardware violation in those individual episodes. They are r0077 seed 8173564, r0083 seed 8173528, r0108 seed 8173524, r0126 seed 8173525 and r0132 seed 8173562. Each checkpoint completes one of 64 starts. The repetition across independent starts demonstrates individual successful executions while the observed rate and other failed traces prevent a generalization claim. Exact outputs are in experiment/ppo_evaluations/completed_contract_replays.json.

The matched 32-start baseline confirms why the smaller step and discrete integrator remain diagnostics. The same 30-plan privileged controller completes 22/32 in registered v2, 9/32 at 1 ms, and 4/32 with the 2 ms discrete solver, each with zero physical-limit violations and stops. Preserve v2 as the setting for the task claim and report its numerical late-arm excursions as a limitation. The refreshed guard dry test gives +26.83 physical plan, -0.79 hold and -6.46 random. Three fixed-plan terminal successes, zero plan hardware violations, zero arm or finger guard cost on the plans. A 7,326-step PPO smoke run with the same guard produces finite outputs. This supports testing the guard as a training change with the next available GPU after its budget.

body.reflection: The 102.55M placement actor makes 64 lifts, 62 turns, 17 controlled carry/release events and one nominal terminal pose across 64 CPU starts. No episode passes all safety checks. The nominal placement, seed 8173531, remains at (0.4535, -0.0481, -0.2935) m for 27.65 s but exceeds a finger limit by 0.02853 rad. The batch has 22 limit violations and 11 stops. This is the strongest observed carry count and motivates a safety-focused continuation if full completion plateaus.

body.text: Finished the placement-only budget at 104,136,936 active steps. Its final 12,994 exploratory full starts give 121 releases and 38 stable short-horizon proxies, versus 120 and 33 in 12,724 previous starts. Stops rise from 1,023 to 1,319, and full 60 s CPU completion stays rare. The final CPU test is in progress. GPU 0 starts a 29M-step limit-guard continuation from the placement checkpoint at 102,549,649, SHA-256 0b2ec332e7ed…. This parent gives 17 supported releases and one 27.65 s upright terminal in 64 CPU starts. Its terminal case has a 0.02853 rad finger excursion and is a failure. The guard uses measured joint and palm margins and terminates training episodes on arm-range excursions at the physics substeps. Bundle this guard with 35 percent of full starts at 60 s because the observed excursion in r0127 comes after the original 15 s horizon. Keep its action box, base rewards, no active mid resets, DR and PPO lineage. The refreshed dry run gives +26.95 plan, -0.79 hold and -6.46 random, two stable plan terminals, no physical-plan violation or guard cost. The exact substep smoke passed 7,236 active steps with no divergence. Predict fewer hardware and replay failures with retained carry and controllable release.

body.reflection: The placement-only trial finishes at 104,136,936 active steps. Final CPU batch has 62 lifts, 31 turns and three supported releases, with zero complete placements across 64 starts. Seventeen limit violation episodes and eleven stops. The 96M and 99M checkpoints provide isolated valid examples, and the 102M checkpoint supplies the guard continuation parent.

body.text: Release audit on three later local batches. The placement parent r0139 matches 17 supported releases at median 0.251 m/s and 4.11 rad/s, with 16 recontacts within 50 ms. Bounded progress at about 93M matches nine releases at median 0.042 m/s and 1.75 rad/s, all recontacting within 50 ms and none achieving a stationary 0.5 s window. Weighted transport at about 96M matches ten releases at 0.197 m/s and 5.57 rad/s, all with rapid recontacts. Slower release alone has not yielded safe withdrawal. The physically settled post-release pool from r0109 is relevant to the next curriculum experiment.

body.reflection: The 93M bounded-progress checkpoint recovers nine supported releases, with 64 lifts and 62 turns across 64 starts. No stable final goal. Eleven limit violation episodes and five stops. Audit release speed and the full horizon before considering it against the incumbent.

body.text: Six-second randomized GPU probes from the r0109 state-only pool separate support transfer and post-release stability. Starting from 48 supported-hand states, the r0108, r0132 and r0139 actors finish resting in 33, 31 and 32 cases. Starting from 48 already released states, they finish resting in 48, 33 and 27 cases respectively, with no stops in that state group. The gates remain full-start 60 s trials. These data suggest that the geometry and speed of the approach to support dominate the failure, and that later placement checkpoints could also benefit from post-release starts. See experiment/settlement_curriculum/actor_diagnostic.json.

r0146 also localizes the bottleneck before support. From 48 upright carry resets, the r0108 actor reaches the carried-entry phase in all 48 but leaves the object resting at six seconds in six. The support-initialized test finishes in 33/48. Prepare state-only resets after opposed upright entry inside the goal, with the body 4–65 mm above standing height and regular measured velocities, so the policy rehearses the actual transition onto the table. The reset keeps the support event uncredited until simulated contact. Use the previously measured physical controller rollouts from r0106, with analytic servo preload and no source action fields. Compare after the active transport budget if its full-start terminal rate stays flat.

The 99.39M transport actor passes package validation at 0.672 ms p99 and records three valid supported releases in 64 local starts. Its two stopped traces fail the state-log contract: in seeds 8173546 and 8173552 the measured arm exceeds its deployed range and the measured palm rotates too quickly at 17.78 and 19.15 s. These errors are consistent with the late excursions under diagnosis. This checkpoint does not go forward to a fresh-start comparison. Limit-margin, transport and reward studies are still active.

body.text: Five iteration uploads from the latest checkpoint comparisons were delayed by a local record-generator variable name collision after the JSON, curves and videos had been written. Fixed the generator and published all five complete artifact sets as r0166 through r0170. The simulations, policies and original evaluation files are unaffected.

In all five contract-clean local placements, the issued wrist rotation differs from the measured palm by at most 0.186 rad before final rest. The nominal placement in r0168 has 0.155 rad maximum before rest and 2.34 rad in the final rest period, with state replay failing at 55.07 s. A 0.36 rad wrist lead projection on the same weights produced six target jumps in the nine-start diagnostic. A second variant adds a 0.08 rad per-action correction bound and eliminates the jumps, but still has seven stops, seven limit violations and seven state replay errors. Both variants lose the nominal complete placement. Retain neither output modification in a gate candidate. Files under experiment/wrist_lead_probe and experiment/wrist_lead_rate_probe.

body.text: The limit-margin branch reaches its 29M continuation budget at 131,551,984. In the final 6,349 stochastic full starts it registers four releases and one terminal proxy. The preceding 6,751 have none. Lift and turn partly recover after early regression, but the late skill remains flat. Start the last-visible pose history experiment on GPU 0 from the new 114,581,837-step bounded-progress parent, SHA-256 532f864ddb55…. It has four contract-clean local completions and a separate arm-range replay error in the batch, so still needs generalization and safety. Continue for 17M steps with the same bounded progress reward, action mapping, full horizon mix, reset pool and DR. Add 33 features derived from the last valid estimated plug pose relative to the palm and measured finger displacement since that estimate. Preserve the parent actor and critic on initialization by zeroing the new columns, and reset optimizer moments for the expanded layers. NumPy and Torch features match within 1e-6, a matching-profile 7,281-step smoke had no divergence, and the package validates at 0.517 ms p99 with no time use. Predict better carry and release information at the r0092 camera losses before support. Keep the bounded, gentle and descent budgets running.

body.reflection: The 114.58M bounded-progress actor completes four of 64 full CPU starts, seeds 8173523, 8173525, 8173538 and 8173539, each with clean v3 replay, no stop or violation, and over 56.5 s of final upright rest. The batch has 62 lifts, 45 turns, four releases, two finger violations and one stop. This is the first checkpoint with more than one valid full result in one batch.

body.text: The second independent 64-start CPU test of the r0183 checkpoint yields one additional full locally clean success, seed 4019658, as well as four contract transcript errors across the batch. No gate submission from this checkpoint. The in-grip turn trace explains a major lost stage: in the original set all 17 lifted-but-unturned episodes achieved sufficient wrist-relative and finger-correlated turn while opposed, but the best blade tilt after the angle tests is median 39.69 degrees. In the independent set 20 of 25 lifted-but-unturned episodes likewise meet the angular excursion tests but have best median tilt 39.86 degrees. A targeted near-upright PPO reward is ready for the next available budget. It pays episode-best elevation only from 45 degrees toward vertical while unsupported, opposed and finger-active with the specified wrist limit. This matches the demonstrated blades-up target before controlled support.

body.reflection: The 108M descent checkpoint lifts and turns on 64 and 59 of 64 CPU starts. One supported release, no final placement, three violation episodes and four stops. Continue the planned reset comparison.

body.text: The gentle transfer run ended at 115,229,103, with one supported release and zero stable results on the final 64 CPU starts. Allocate GPU 1 to a single reward change from r0183, a bounded episode-best upright blade potential during active unsupported opposition with wrist rotation within 65 degrees. The r0184 analysis found enough active wrist-relative turn but median minimum blade tilt near 40 degrees in 17 of 17 primary and 20 of 25 confirmation-set traces missing the turn. The reward dry check credits the 24 physical plans by 2.57 on average and gives zero extra reward to hold and random. The 48-environment rollout produced 9,352 finite active steps. Keep the previous 35 percent full runs, task box, reset pool and other reward terms. Train through 128,581,837 and predict more qualifying turns and then more supported releases from 60 s deployment starts.

Bounded progress reached 119,231,301 steps with one nominal placement among 64 development starts. The last three training bins of about 2.8M steps recorded roughly 17 full-horizon proxy successes per 2,800 to 2,900 starts each, and deterministic completion peaked earlier at r0183. GPU 2 will test PPO entropy weight 0.004 versus 0.012 from r0183 through 127,581,837 active steps. Reward, start mixture, architecture, sensors and action interface stay fixed. Hypothesis: after reaching controlled release, lower exploration pressure will help keep the deterministic policy near the reproducible acquisition and carry behavior. Compare both qualifying turns and full placements, along with stops and replay errors. Discontinue this setting if deterministic completion and hardware checks fail to improve.

body.reflection: Airborne-descent comparison from the complete range of full v3 starts. More turns than the parent, zero supported release at this checkpoint, six violations and five stops.

body.text: The main gap at the best bounded-progress checkpoints is the transfer, with the object often finishing upright anyway. At r0183 the final resting goal alone holds in 58/64 CPU episodes. Of those, 15 fail the strict turn, nine fail the transition onto support and 30 lose table support before the hand opens. Only four pass the described transfer and all other tests. In r0194, 59/64 finish upright but only three pass the full motion. At r0201 all 64 finish upright, but 37 tilt beyond 20 degrees near initial support and 22 lose support before opening after an otherwise qualifying turn and carry. Matched full-start nominal GPU replay of r0183 gives the training terminal surrogate in 58/64 and the frozen staged criteria in 5/64. body.text: The blade-upright branch finished at 128,582,294, with no qualifying releases in its latest evaluated checkpoint and a terminal surrogate rate of 35.4 percent in its final 2.8M training steps. The airborne-descent branch also finished, with zero terminal proxies in its last 4,175 full starts. With GPU 1 free, rerun the gentle touchdown reward from r0201 rather than from the early transport parent used in r0120. r0201 already reaches the upright resting endpoint across all 64 development starts, so the near-support penalty and quiet-support bonus can act where contact continuity fails. Only the reward differs from the r0201 parent. The matched dry check scores +25.92 physical, -0.79 hold and -2.18 random, with one physical terminal outcome. Train 10M more active steps to 133,685,782, checkpoint every 2M, and predict fewer loss-of-support and blade-tilt failures. The final gate for the current eligible incumbent stays on schedule.

body.reflection: The strict transfer replica at 119.23M completes one nominal episode and incurs 17 hardware violations and one stop on the full set. Replay checks qualify the completion.

body.text: The pose-history strict-transfer run reached its 130,732,080-step cap. The last two 2.8M-step bins had 20/2,896 then 29/2,953 surrogate completions, and median PPO KL stayed near 0.021. The last three CPU checkpoints had one, zero and one nominal placement, with no sustained improvement. Test optimizer learning rate 0.00012 instead of 0.00027 for the same 7M-step continuation from r0201, leaving curriculum, architecture, strict transfer reward and action bounds identical. Predict that smaller updates preserve more of r0201's clean acquisition and carried entry as the contact-continuity reward changes what pays at touchdown. Use GPU 0 through 130,685,782 active steps. The final gate already runs independently on GPU 3.

body.text: The loss-of-support trace does not always include a visible upward bounce. Across 30 r0183 cases with a support break before opening, the median time from first unsupported sample to next support is 16.7 ms. The median plug centre at the highest sample during that gap is 1.13 mm below its centre at initial contact, and median vertical velocity at the first lost-support row is -0.030 m/s. At r0201 the corresponding medians over 22 gaps are 16.7 ms, 0.68 mm below initial contact, and +0.039 m/s. This is a break in modeled surface contact during settling. The exact geometric/contact trajectories depend on compliance and friction, while the frozen criterion consistently requires support through opening. See experiment/media/support_recoil_summary.json.

body.text: The strict-transfer replica completed its 6.5M-step budget at a surrogate rate near one percent, with zero full success at the final frozen CPU checkpoint. Use the freed GPU 2 on a focused test for the other dominant r0201 transfer failure, 37/64 episodes tilting beyond 20 degrees near support after upright carry. From the same r0201 parent add only a modest pose cost during carry and supported hand contact inside the goal and within 65 mm of standing height. The cost is zero at up to 10 degrees and rises to 0.08 per step at 35 degrees. The 24-start check gives +25.24 for physical plans, -0.79 for hold and -2.18 random, with two physical terminal proxies. The exact-configuration smoke completes 9,405 active steps with zero divergent worlds. Continue through 129,685,782 active steps. Predict reduced tilt loss during supported transfer at similar stage and hardware counts. The gate criteria stay frozen.

body.reflection: Repeated strict transfer with smaller PPO update at 129.90M. Full-start counts retain 56 turns but no release. One hardware violation, no stop.

body.text: In 199 transfer events audited across r0183, r0194, r0201 and r0206, neither the event nor the preceding 350 ms contains a valid object pose estimate. This includes all 12 clean completion events in those primary sets. Median pose age at those completions is 0.77 to 0.79 s. In a local 2 ms feasibility-controller sample, 31 qualifying transfers also have median camera visibility zero during the 350 ms before support, with peak visibility no higher than 5.9 percent. We will measure a counterfactual with occlusion disabled in the camera model on two already scored actors, using the same seeds and all other sensor parameters and physics. It is diagnostic only. The feasibility and task suites still use their original configurations, and the deployable actor receives only estimated poses.

Test the 131,848,972-step gentle-touchdown checkpoint in a fresh paired task gate. It has six v3-clean full completions and 175 qualifying turns across two fixed sets totaling 192 deployment starts. Five episodes violate hardware limits, one stops, and two other traces have state replay errors. The package itself validates with act p99 0.568 ms. The late transfer gain is repeatable locally while safety remains uncertain. Its gate is a test of that observed gain and the paired hardware restriction. Keep the current incumbent unless this candidate clears the actual gate.

body.reflection: Confirm the gentle-touchdown checkpoint on the independent 128-start set shared with r0199. Four nominal full placements and 117 turns. Replay each completion and measure all hardware violations.

body.text: In the matched camera counterfactual, forcing visibility to one while retaining sensor delay and noise yields two full staged episodes for r0183 instead of four and zero for r0201 in both conditions. Hardware violations rise from two to six for r0183 and from zero to two for r0201. This intervention also changes the observation histories the learned policies were trained on. It does not isolate the value of fresh pose information for a trained estimator, but removing occlusion at inference alone does not solve transfer. The contact loss is best handled by improving the learned sequence and by learning robust grip state under deployment occlusion. See experiment/media/{progress114m,anchor123m}_unoccluded.json.

body.hypothesis: Bounded progress and pose memory reach upright goal entry. Adding low-speed touchdown and a settled-support bonus to the strong pose-history parent should improve continuous leftward carry and supported release.
body.observed: In r0241 seed 70092683 at 56.20 s, the hand is still around the tilted plug. It finishes touching the hand and stops short at y=-0.2052 m. Seed 2116557119 shows the same continuing grip adjustments at 48.50 s and ends at y=-0.1807 m.

body.text: The fresh paired gate r0255 for r0246/r0253 stops before comparison. In seed 1059961262 the logged hand and arm ranges leave tolerance and the palm reaches 12.17 rad/s at 27.60 s, above 11.25. It returns no new montage. The latest rendered evidence remains r0241. In a local replay of the same checkpoint, seed 9127213 shows J5 moving from -2.57 to -3.135 rad at 10.97 s with the plug resting on the table and no hand contact. The deployed lower J5 limit is -2.90. Test only a terminal -4 reward and episode termination for the already-monitored GPU arm excursion beyond 0.05 rad at a 2 ms substep. This keeps nominal action mapping and skips the dense margin terms that disrupted acquisition in r0185. Start from the exact r0246 parent snapshot and train 4M more active steps. The dry check yields +30.80 physical, -0.79 hold and -2.34 random, four physical terminal proxies and no physical arm penalty. The smoke test processed 9,405 active steps without divergence. Compare joint excursions and supported release on the fixed full starts. Do not replace r0078 without a passing paired gate.

Operator extends the run budget by ten hours. The original start is 2026-11-19T00:57:02Z and the new deadline reported by the time tool is 2026-11-19T18:57:02Z. Retain all prior records, including the failed final r0241/r0243 and state-log failure r0255. Continue with two measured lines of work. First, test physically faithful arm dynamics under the existing frozen criteria, including contact-only external torque per hardware/ARM.md and the measured delayed joint response. A changed simulator will need its own recorded validation, suites and renewed feasibility proof. Second, use r0203/r0234/r0249 to improve training reward and state coverage for controlled support transfer under occlusion, with full-start checks throughout. Preserve the present v2 incumbent while comparing the alternatives. Reserve more than an hour near the extended deadline for fresh gates, verdict and reflection.

Arm response audit after r0255. In sim v2 the reference-velocity term D times q_ref_dot is added as external generalized force beyond the wrist motor effort limiter. At the model's 180 degree/s joint command limit, this term is 36 N m on J5-J7, twice their 18 N m model actuator limit. The stop estimator also uses total constraint torque, including joint-limit reactions; hardware/ARM.md specifies environment contact wrenches. Test a two-by-two diagnostic with the damping reference inside the motor effort limiter and a contact-only torque halt, separately and jointly. Keep joint ranges, IK, timestep, geometry, sensor, evaluator state checks and task criteria. Predict reduced measured arm excursion and fewer false torque halts without reducing physical carry feasibility. The v2 suite stays frozen.

body.reflection: First terminal arm-excursion guard checkpoint, 52 qualifying turns, no later stages, one violation and one stop. Evaluate the subsequent checkpoints.

body.text: The 24-start stress comparison reproduces all six nominal stages of the v2 soft policy and its faults. With damping reference inside the arm effort limiter, the same starts have zero measured arm excursions, zero hardware-violation episodes and zero stops versus one excursion, five violations and one stop in v2. There is one full completion instead of six. Using contact-only torque yields the same outcomes as each corresponding motor variant here. These are outcomes on a selected stress set, not a deployment estimate. The change to actuators appears to remove an important integration fault and changes the manipulation dynamics. Test the existing physical-plan controller on both variants before selecting any simulation change.

Start a 25M-step v2 PPO comparison from r0201 on GPU 1. Keep the initial actor, optimizer, start mixture and strict-transfer phase tracker of r0211, and add one physical handover objective with two bounded terms. Aligned descent, low object speed and increasing vertical table load earn up to 6 per episode, with no credit for repeated motion. Two consecutive control samples of quiet continuous loaded support with hand contact pay a 5-point bonus once. A static test gives table load of 1.000 plug weights across all 16 randomized worlds. Dry returns on 24 starts are +24.08 physical, -0.79 hold and -2.18 random, and the proposal adds +0.99 measured progress for the physical plans. The 11-start targeted check adds +0.51 on average. No dry plan earns the new quiet bonus yet. The physical progress term provides a dense signal while learning that transition. Predict more continuously supported openings and full completions from real v3 starting conditions without trading away the turn. Score full CPU episodes every about 3M and retain exact replays. The motor-limited simulation is still experimental.

The new handover bank adds 518 physically reached states from 128 training-only position/yaw draws using the r0201 and r0246 actors. It includes 388 opposed airborne states in three approach bands and 130 supported states with hand contact. After 0.10 s in randomized GPU holds, 375 airborne resets still have unsupported opposition and 118 supported resets still touch the table, with zero stops or violations. Every new reset has a preceding valid estimated pose. Train two 24M-step v2 continuations with the same load-transfer reward, state bins, randomization, network and r0201 parent. The sole paired difference is initializing the actor's existing pose memory with the last valid estimated grip pose and preceding proprioception at those curriculum resets. Every full deployment start uses ordinary memory reset. No recorded policy targets or human finger actions enter the records or the weights. Record clean full-start transfer and hardware outcomes for both.

simulator.name: MuJoCo
simulator.gpu_backend: MuJoCo Warp GPU solver with matched model and commands, using float32 dynamics.

scene.model: Full provided Marvin Wuji MJCF, both arms/hands and original collision geometry, with a single plug, table, floor, and column.

plug.state_frame: Housing centre, +Z toward blade tips, +Y across the blade gap. Identity object/body frame.
plug.geometry: Station housing and two blade OBJ parts from given/recon. Exact specified dimensions and axes.
plug.physical_prior: The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
plug.contact: Housing and two blades have separate convex collision meshes. Elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solref 0.012 s / damping ratio 1, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001].

reference.method: White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

body.arm: Published 100 Hz palm clamp and jump stop, measured-seed DLS IK with the 5 degree ranges, delayed 100 Hz joint reference and velocity, and the provided arm capsules. The position actuator receives q_ref + (D/K) q_ref_dot so velocity tracking effort is counted inside each motor's effort cap. Compensate modeled bias minus gravity compensation separately. Use only contact EFC rows for the right arm or hand against table, plug, column or parked arm to estimate external torque with J transpose f. The existing 30 ms estimated torque filter and 20 Nm halt operate on that signal.
body.hand: Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise.
body.sensor: Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.

body.text: Feasibility r0271 proves task suite v3 on 25 of 32 fresh starts with zero hardware violations or stops. I reviewed the two failure and two success montages. The failures in seeds 1101195590 and 1564294741 are both upright and hands-off by 17.70 s, with passive rotation of 27.5 and 33 degrees versus the 25-degree allowance. The success examples 1693345725 and 484050708 retain upright rest for about 50 s and measure 23.4 and 24.1 degrees of passive turn. Start 24M active PPO steps now from r0201 on GPU 3 with the motor-limited station. Match the handover comparison on GPU 0 in curriculum, actor, reward and optimizer. The only change is the recorded physics. The 48-world smoke produces finite PPO updates without nonfinite worlds. Predict fewer measured arm excursions while preserving genuine handover performance. Run full CPU v3 units every 3M steps and exact replay before any candidate gate.

reward_terms.name: wrist_reference

reward_terms.name: active_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Pay for episode-best combined blade elevation and relative rotation while unsupported, opposed and actively moving the fingers.

reward_terms.name: passive_rotation
reward_terms.formula: Variation of relative orientation under opposed contact with nearly stationary fingers

reward_terms.name: turn
reward_terms.formula: Completes at least 50 degrees of wrist-relative turn while opposed with blades within 20 degrees of up At most once per episode across retries.

reward_terms.name: carry_progress

reward_terms.name: place_progress

Carry advances to descent at least 15 mm inside the zone. Credit positive physical progress only beyond the prior episode best. The same excursion earns once across retries.

reward_terms.name: support_transfer
reward_terms.formula: First table support with hand contact following the turn and carried goal entry At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: release
reward_terms.formula: After controlled support transfer, stable upright table support with hand contact released At most once per episode across retries. Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: durable_goal
reward_terms.formula: Maintains terminal goal for 0.5 s, penalty for subsequent disturbance Require upright carried entry in the turned grip, continuous hand contact until the table takes the load, and continuous upright table support until opening. Check this sequence at every 60 Hz sample.

reward_terms.name: drop
reward_terms.formula: Loses the opposed airborne plug before support Also penalize and reset the grasp attempt if the transport returns to support before entry or loses opposition for two steps.

reward_terms.name: time_and_control
reward_terms.formula: Living cost, small action term, hand/table cost, and safety penalty

reward_terms.name: leftward_progress

reward_terms.name: settling_progress

reward_terms.name: hand_clearance

reward_terms.name: recontact

reward_terms.name: terminal_goal

body.text: Use r0246 as the first task-suite v3 baseline. Against the same 64 local starts as its v2 record it now has 63 lifts, 59 turns, four full placements, zero hardware violations and zero stops. All 64 state-contract checks pass. The weights and interface are the archived v2 PPO export. This isolates the effect of the corrected arm dynamics before v3 PPO adaptation. Evaluate it on the gate's fresh starts, with the current criteria and timing checks.

body.text: Fresh task gate r0287 ends before comparison with an observed and logged finger joint beyond the deployed range tolerance. It produces no new montage. The last review r0271 shows table delivery after finger motion, with passive slip as its main failure. The motor-limited station clears the old arm faults in local replay, but a finger integration fault remains on some starts. The public hand specification says the simulated joints stop at the deployed limits. Test finer 1 ms integration, a 2 ms unilateral limit solver time constant at that substep, and a small pre-contact limit margin separately from the current v3 settings. All diagnoses use the same joint ranges, motor limits, sensors and evaluator checks. body.text: Finger-limit integration controls an important part of the remaining failures. On the same 24 selected early-v3 policy starts, current 2 ms physics records 13 hardware violations, 1 ms with the same limit settings records five, 1 ms with a 2 ms solver limit time constant records zero, and 2 ms with a 4 mrad anticipatory limit margin records four. Test the firmer 1 ms integration with a stronger learned policy and with the prior multi-plan feasibility controller before deciding whether to change the recorded simulator again.
